data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts using a checklist will produce more reliable judgments than a single expert using intuition for objectively verifiable tasks, provided the task is decomposable into discrete, independent criteria.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires non-linear synthesis or 'gestalt' recognition that cannot be decomposed into a checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is poorly designed, omitting critical variables that the expert's intuition implicitly captures.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'training' of non-experts introduces a shared systemic bias (correlated error) that outweighs the benefit of redundancy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The panel reduces the variance of the outcome by replacing a single point of failure (the expert's System 1 cognitive bias or fatigue) with a redundant, System 2-driven process. Reliability is gained through the 'wisdom of the crowd' filtered by a rigorous protocol, which cancels out individual random errors that the expert's intuition might systematize.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
